title: Cockpit geography · displays · first look at the start flow
focus: Nobody hunts for a switch twice. Tonight is geography and screens, not handling.

blocks.title: Pre-brief with your partner
items: Agree roles — one flying, one reading the checklist. Not both poking.
Agree the swap point: halfway, then the other seat for the second pass.
Challenge-and-response out loud, every time. Silent button-pushing is a habit you'll unlearn at the GND 6 SIT.
When one of you catches the other's error, say what the trap was — that's the part that sticks.

blocks.title: Cockpit geography — quiz, not a tour
items: Partner reads a switch name at random; you put a finger on it without narrating the search.
Engine start switches · START buttons · booster pumps · IPS rotary
Fuel crossfeed · GEN 1 / GEN 2 · battery master · GPU
Flight Controller buttons — you'll need these cold for EDM later
AP / YD engage, TCS, and the AP Disengage switch on BOTH wheels
Flap lever and detents · airbrake · gear lever
Guarded handles: emergency brake, engine fire, evacuation
Transponder panel
Verify the DU colour conventions against the real screens — red, amber, magenta, cyan, green, white, grey
Second pass through the whole list. The savings come from the second pass.

blocks.title: Displays and CAS — the best use of a GFS
items: Which AGM drives which DUs, and how many unique images one AGM can produce
Tell a DU failure from an AGM failure — the guide calls this essential
Single DU failed → corrective action. Perform it, don't just read it.
DU 1 and DU 2 both showing a large X → actions in order
Two DUs failed and off → what appears where, for each pair
CAS levels: colour, master light, aural for each
Walk the aural priority ladder out loud; name what is always first
Mute an uncommanded AP disconnect — and name what will NOT mute it

blocks.title: Power-up and ground power
items: GPU voltage check BEFORE connecting — say the number first, then verify
GPU load limits, initial surge vs continuous
Battery minimums for start; minimum volts to charge, maximum volts to charge
Battery temperature limits for flight
Run the cockpit prep flow with the checklist, challenge-and-response

blocks.title: First look at the start flow
items: RH start: engine switch to RUN, confirm booster pump, confirm NO fuel pressure CAS, START press
Watch the sequence: START ON at press, inverse video at ~10% N2, N1 increasing, parameters to IDL
Say the ground idle targets from memory BEFORE looking at the gauges, then compare
Confirm GEN 2 takes over and is supplying the aircraft
The moisture note: TAT or reported OAT below the ice line with visible moisture → IPS rotary to AUTO/NAI
LH start — and the trap: the right engine must exit QPM and be at Ground Idle first
Have your partner try to walk you into starting the left engine with the right still in QPM. Catch it.

blocks.title: Emergency controls — locate only
items: Touch, name, move on. Do NOT run these to standard tonight — the gate is GND 8.
Engine fire handles
Emergency brake
Crew oxygen masks — Cabin Altitude, Emergency Descent and Smoke all start here
Evacuation controls
Goal: at the GND 8 SIT your hands already know the geography, so you can spend that session on the words.

blocks.title: Swap seats — repeat the start flow
items: Other pilot flies: power-up → both starts → ground idle
Skip the geography quiz if the first pass ran clean

blocks.title: Debrief — write three lists
items: Switches either of you hunted for → straight into tomorrow's review
Flow steps that came out wrong or out of order → drill those cards tonight
Questions for the instructor tomorrow — GFS behaviour that didn't match the cards is worth asking about

title: Avionics · Master Warning · Electrical
focus: Trigger the failures rather than reading about them. Reversion is muscle memory, not trivia.

blocks.title: Pre-brief
items: Roles and swap point
Tonight's standard: every CAS answer stated before the screen is consulted

blocks.title: The CAS ladder, out loud
items: Warning / Caution / Advisory / Status — colour, master light, aural for each
Sort order between colour groups, and ordering within a group
How many messages display at once, and what happens past that
Recite the aural priority ladder top to bottom without prompting
Partner names an aural; you give its relative priority. Then reverse.

blocks.title: Aural priority under a pile-up
items: Two aurals active at once — how the system decides, and what is always first
Mute an uncommanded AP disconnect; name what will NOT mute it
How EGPWS and TCAS aurals reach you relative to CAS aurals
TAWS alert and TCAS alert together — what happens

blocks.title: Display failures and reversion — performed
items: Sketch the AGM → DU architecture on paper from memory, then verify
Inject a single DU failure and perform the corrective action
Inject the DU 1 + DU 2 double failure; perform the actions in order
Two DUs off — confirm what appears where for each pair
Name both display monitors and what each one checks
Required action for Check Pilot PFD / Check Copilot PFD / Check Engine Display

blocks.title: Swap seats — reversion again
items: Other pilot performs all three reversion cases
Partner calls the CAS aural priorities while the other reverts

blocks.title: Debrief
items: Any reversion step performed out of order → drill tonight
Any aural you couldn't place in the ladder → drill tonight

items: Any FMA state you misread → drill tonight

title: SIT day — normal procedures, cockpit prep to shutdown

blocks.title: Pre-brief
items: Roles and swap point

blocks.title: Run the whole profile again, for time
